title: Rational polynomial evaluation unfolds one degree at a time
statement: For a coefficient sequence p, degree index n and point x, evaluating p at x through degree n+1 equals (evaluating through degree n) plus the degree-n term p(n) * x^n.

formal.statement: theorem Rat.polyEval_succ : ((x0 : ((x0 : AxNat) -> Rat)) -> ((x1 : AxNat) -> ((x2 : Rat) -> Eq.{1} Rat (Rat.polyEval x0 (AxNat.succ x1) x2) (Rat.add (Rat.polyEval x0 x1 x2) (Rat.mul (x0 x1) (Rat.pow x2 x1))))))

evidence.supports: Rat.polyEval_succ is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with the type recorded in formal.statement.
evidence.checker_command: cargo run -q --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --example theorem_dependency_inventory -- Rat.polyEval_succ 2>/dev/null | grep -cE '^Rat\.polyEval_succ[[:space:]]'
evidence.notes: `build_rat_prelude` admits Rat.polyEval_succ through the trusted `Kernel::add_declaration` gate, which re-checks the proof term against the stated type, so a line in this tool's output for the exact name is a machine-checked proof having been admitted. `theorem_dependency_inventory` exits non-zero for a named filter that matches nothing (a deleted theorem cannot read as a re-derived one), and `grep -c` (never `-q`) both avoids a SIGPIPE-under-pipefail false negative and independently asserts the exact tab-anchored line is present -- two ways the same absence would be caught. `--release` is MANDATORY: this tool now also builds `creal`/`complex`/`cpoint`, which recurse deep enough in a debug build to overflow the default thread stack (measured: release exits 0 with 1092 theorems, debug SIGABRTs at 134) -- the same resource-limit gotcha already documented for `prelude_theorem_inventory --include-constructed`.

evidence.supports: axiom_footprint: [] -- the Rat prelude's trusted surface is empty
evidence.notes: `nat_axiom_inventory` builds the Rat environment as its own group and reports `rat: axiom=0 opaque=0 quotient=0 total_trusted=0` (re-measured on this tree). That bounds every individual Rat theorem's footprint by [], since a theorem cannot depend on a trusted declaration the environment does not contain -- and the enumeration covers Axiom, Opaque AND Quotient, not just Declaration::Axiom, because Opaque has no proof body and Quotient admits Quot.sound. `--require-axiom-free <name>` is an error (not a silent pass/zero) for a prelude this run never built, which is what makes `rat` here a claim rather than an absence.
